en.meaning: The Blessed Lord says: See, Partha, my forms in hundreds and thousands, diverse, divine, and of many colors and shapes.

en.intro: Krishna stands ready to reveal more than Arjuna ever asked for. Listen to what he asks him to look at.
en.body: The Blessed Lord says: See, Partha, my forms in hundreds and thousands, diverse, divine, and of many colors and shapes. Krishna addresses him as Partha, son of Pritha, and tells him to see hundreds of thousands of divine forms. The word rupani, forms, shows this is not one body but a universe of shapes and colors. He then lists the Adityas, Vasus, and Rudras, showing Arjuna the gods themselves gathered in one vision.

issues: meaning_changed: "मेरे सैकड़ोंहजारों विविध, दिव्य रूप, अनेक वर्ण और आकार वाले, तू देख।" (The Hindi translation drops the word 'hundreds' (शतशः / सैकड़ों) and 'thousands' (सहस्रशः / हजारों), merging them into 'hundreds of thousands' (लाखों). While the English meaning correctly lists hundreds and thousands, the Hindi meaning changes the quantity from a list of hundreds and thousands to a single number, 'hundreds of thousands', which is not the exact meaning of the Sanskrit.)

unsupported: "कृष्ण अब अर्जुन से कुछ ऐसा दिखाने को तैयार हैं जिसकी उन्होंने कल्पना भी नहीं की थी।" (The source text (verse 5) only contains Krishna telling Arjuna to look at his forms. The claim that Krishna is ready to show something Arjuna 'never imagined' is an unsupported factual claim about Arjuna's state of mind and anticipation, which is not present in the verse.)
